{{Short description|Austrian mathematician}}
[[File:Harald Niederreiter.jpg|thumb|Harald Niederreiter in [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]], 2013]]
'''Harald G. Niederreiter''' (born June 7, 1944) is an Austrian mathematician known for his work in [[discrepancy theory]], [[algebraic geometry]], [[quasi-Monte Carlo method]]s, and [[cryptography]].

==Education and career==
Niederreiter was born on June 7, 1944, in [[Vienna]], and grew up in [[Salzburg]].<ref name="shortbio">{{citation
 | last1 = Ding | first1 = Cunsheng
 | last2 = Xing | first2 = Chaoping
 | doi = 10.1016/j.jco.2003.12.001
 | issue = 2–3
 | journal = Journal of Complexity
 | mr = 2067423
 | pages = 134–136
 | title = A short biography of Harald Niederreiter
 | volume = 20
 | year = 2004| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref><ref name="highlights">{{citation|contribution=Some highlights of Harald Niederreiter's work|title=Applied Algebra and Number Theory: Essays in Honor of Harald Niederreiter on the occasion of his 70th birthday|first1=Gerhard|last1=Larcher|first2=Friedrich|last2=Pillichshammer|first3=Arne|last3=Winterhof|first4=Chaoping|last4=Xing|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2014|isbn=9781107074002|pages=1–21|arxiv=1407.3630|bibcode=2014arXiv1407.3630L}}.</ref> He began studying mathematics at the [[University of Vienna]] in 1963,<ref name="shortbio"/><ref name="highlights"/> and finished his doctorate there in 1969, with a thesis on [[Discrepancy theory|discrepancy]] in [[Compact group|compact]] [[abelian group]]s supervised by [[Edmund Hlawka]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=22632}}</ref>
He began his academic career as an assistant professor at the University of Vienna, but soon moved to [[Southern Illinois University]].<ref name="shortbio"/><ref name="highlights"/> During this period he also visited the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]], [[Institute for Advanced Study]], and [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref name="highlights"/> In 1978 he moved again, becoming the head of a new mathematics department at the [[University of the West Indies]] in [[Jamaica]]. In 1981 he returned to Austria for a post at the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]], where from 1989 to 2000 he served as director of the Institutes of Information Processing and Discrete Mathematics. In 2001 he became a professor at the [[National University of Singapore]].<ref name="shortbio"/><ref name="highlights"/> In 2009 he returned to Austria again, to the Johann Radon Institute for Computational and Applied Mathematics of the Austrian Academy of Sciences. He also worked from 2010 to 2011 as a professor at the [[King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals]] in [[Saudi Arabia]].<ref name="highlights"/>

==Research==
Niederreiter's initial research interests were in the [[abstract algebra]] of [[abelian group]]s and [[finite field]]s, subjects also represented by his later book ''Finite Fields'' (with Rudolf Lidl, 1983).<ref name="shortbio"/> From his doctoral thesis onwards, he also incorporated [[discrepancy theory]] and the theory of [[Delone set|uniformly distributed sets]] in [[metric space]]s into his study of these subjects.<ref name="highlights"/>

In 1970, Niederreiter began to work on [[numerical analysis]] and [[random number generation]], and in 1974 he published the book ''Uniform Distribution of Sequences''. Combining his work on pseudorandom numbers with the [[Monte Carlo method]], he did pioneering research in the [[quasi-Monte Carlo method]] in the late 1970s, and again later published a book on the topic, ''Random Number Generation and Quasi-Monte Carlo Methods'' (1995).<ref name="shortbio"/><ref name="highlights"/>

Niederreiter's interests in pseudorandom numbers also led him to study [[stream cipher]]s in the 1980s, and this interest branched out into other areas of [[cryptography]] such as [[public key cryptography]]. The [[Niederreiter cryptosystem]], an encryption system based on [[error-correcting code]]s that can also be used for [[digital signature]]s, was developed by him in 1986.<ref name="shortbio"/> His work in cryptography is represented by his book ''Algebraic Geometry in Coding Theory and Cryptography'' (with C. P. Xing, 2009).<ref name="highlights"/>

Returning to pure mathematics, Niederreiter has also made contributions to [[algebraic geometry]] with the discovery of many dense curves over finite fields,<ref name="shortbio"/> and published the book ''Rational Points on Curves over Finite Fields: Theory and Applications'' (with C. P. Xing, 2001).<ref name="highlights"/>

==Awards and honors==
Niederreiter is a member of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]] and the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]. In 1998 he was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]],<ref>{{cite book|author=Niederreiter, Harald|chapter=Nets, (''t,s'')-sequences, and algebraic curves over finite fields with many rational points|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=377–386|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011594000}}</ref> and won the [[Kardinal Innitzer Prize]].<ref name="shortbio"/><ref name="highlights"/> He became a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2013.<ref name="highlights"/>

Niederreiter's book ''Random Number Generation and Quasi-Monte Carlo Methods'' won the Outstanding Simulation Publication Award.<ref name="shortbio"/>

In 2014, a workshop in honor of Niederreiter's 70th birthday was held at the Johann Radon Institute for Computational and Applied Mathematics of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]],<ref>[https://www.ricam.oeaw.ac.at/events/workshops/hn70/ Workshop on the Occasion of Harald Niederreiter's 70th Birthday: Applications of Algebra and Number Theory], retrieved 2015-07-18.</ref> and a [[Festschrift]] was published in his honor.<ref>{{citation|title=Applied Algebra and Number Theory: Essays in Honor of Harald Niederreiter on the occasion of his 70th birthday|editor1-first=Gerhard|editor1-last=Larcher|editor2-first=Friedrich|editor2-last=Pillichshammer|editor3-first=Arne|editor3-last=Winterhof|editor4-first=Chaoping|display-editors = 3 |editor4-last=Xing|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2014|isbn=9781107074002}}.</ref>
